item.title: How Samsung's Galaxy Watch 8 measures your antioxidant levels - Engadget
item.summary: # How Samsung's Galaxy Watch 8 measures your antioxidant levels We think it's kind of neat. Samsung's [Galaxy Watch 8](https://www.engadget.com/wearables/samsung-galaxy-watch-8-hands-on-new-look-new-ai-and-new-antioxidants-140039472.html) can already track your heart rate, sleep and workouts. But that's not enough information about you, apparently. Its Antioxidant Index turns a five-second thumb scan into a score from 0 to 100. The watch isn't measuring all of the antioxidants in your body. Instead, it estimates carotenoids, pigments with antioxidant properties found in yellow, orange and green fruits and vegetables that can build up in your skin. Samsung uses that reading as an indicator of fruit and vegetable intake, though the company says UV exposure, alcohol and stress can also affect the score. ## How the sensor reads your skin To take a measurement, remove the Galaxy Watch 8, open Samsung Health on the watch, select Antioxidant Index and tap Measure before pressing your thumb against the BioActive Sensor on the back.
